identity.instrumentFamily: DigCompEdu Check-In / PeerJ2024 published higher-education English survey dated 2023-06-02

construct.constructDefinition: Assessment: self-reported digital teaching engagement/practice in the published higher-education survey. Area raw sum, not observed competence or teaching quality.

population.populationNotes: Adults teaching in higher/further education. Source study: health-sciences faculty; this separated area has no independently established administration validation. Not a school/student or validated Chinese version.

administration.timeFrame: Current practice; long-term professional goals (no fixed retrospective day window).
layoutConstraints: Keep source order and all five item-specific options. Score options in printed ascending order 0,1,2,3,4.
Prefer all six areas in original 22-item order; separated-area validity is not established.
Complete-case raw sum only. Any missing/invalid answer yields no area score; no imputation. This missingness policy is a project choice.
Do not derive global A1–C2 levels from an area or from this combination; no cross-tool total.
Estimated time is a project estimate.

intendedUses.notes: Developmental reflection on self-reported practice; area separation not independently validated.
Source study concerns higher-education health-sciences faculty, not K12 or an objectively measured performance test.

options.label: I do not monitor students’ progress
I do monitor students' progress regularly, but not with digital means
Sometimes I use a digital tool, e.g. a quiz, to check on students' progress
I use a variety of digital tools to monitor student progress
I systematically use a variety of digital tools to monitor student progress
These data are not available and/or it is not my responsibility to analyse them
I only analyse academically relevant data, e.g. performance and grades
I also consider data on student activity and behaviour to identify students who need additional support
I regularly screen all available evidence to identify students who need additional support
I systematically analyse data and intervene in a timely manner
Feedback is not necessary in my work environment
I do provide feedback to students, but not in digital format
Sometimes I use digital ways of providing feedback, e.g. automatic scores in online quizzes, comments or "likes" in online environments
I use a variety of digital ways of providing feedback
I systematically use digital approaches to provide feedback

items.content: I use digital assessment formats to monitor student progress

I analyse all data available to me to timely identify students who need additional support "Data" includes: students' engagement, performance, grades, attendance; activities and social interactions in (online) environments;"Students who need additional support" are: students who are at risk of dropping out or underperforming; students who have learning disorders or specific learning needs, students who lack transversal skills, e.g. social, verbal or study skills.
I use digital technologies to provide effective feedback

scores.label: Assessment (area raw sum)
scores.description: 3 item-specific 0–4 responses summed without reversing; range 0–12. Descriptive self-report, not a validated standalone proficiency grade.

interpretations.headline: Assessment: reflect on your current practice
interpretations.summary: These answers describe your own perception of practice in assessment. A higher raw sum means you selected options describing more digital engagement; it does not establish observed competence, student outcomes or teaching quality. Consider which practices worked for your learners and which depended on time, access or institutional support. Fewer opportunities to use technology do not make you a less capable teacher. There is no norm-based high/low category here.

guidance.text: Try one low-stakes check for understanding and give one specific next-step comment; use only data you are authorised to access.
If access, workload or support is limiting your options, record one specific need and discuss a feasible next step with an appropriate colleague or support team.

limitations: Higher-education English survey published by Ersoy et al. (2024), dated 2023-06-02; this is not the original school Check-In, SELFIEforTEACHERS32 or a validated Chinese edition.
Area separation and this complete-case missingness policy are project adaptations. Prefer the full original 22-item sequence; no standalone area validation or norm is claimed.
Self-report is affected by opportunities, resources and interpretation. Do not use for diagnosis, performance ranking, teacher accountability or unsupported comparisons.
report.disclaimer: Teacher developmental reflection only. Missing/invalid answers mean insufficient evidence for an area score; do not substitute zero. Background and A1–C2 self-positioning forms have no calculated scores. Results remain subject to existing recipient and publication permissions.

instruction.text: Please consider where you stand in view of the following long-term goals. The answer options are organised by increasing level of engagement. Please choose the option that best reflects your current practice. This is the Assessment area of the published higher-education survey. Each item has its own five options; keep their order. All area items are needed for a descriptive raw sum. Prefer the full 22-item sequence. This is developmental self-reflection, not an observed competence test.
instruction.source: First three sentences condensed from the source area instructions; remaining administration, scoring and limitation wording added by the project.
